The earlier version put a space before every capital, including one right after a space, so `"Hello World"` came out with a double space. The lookbehind `(?<=\w)` only inserts a space when a word character comes before the capital, which fixes that case. Single words like `"Python"` are still unchanged.

```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<=\w)(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```
